g.text: The checkpoint pair, and what full versus incremental uploads
full 14 vs incremental 8 entry-uploads at k=3 · stale offset costs 22
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = which group it belongs to
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the keys state is held per. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: CHK — the index the checkpoint in this chapter was taken at. CHK = 4
13 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the window holding et.
15 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
16 // primitive: contains(xs, x) — is x in xs? contains([1,2], 2) = true
17 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest event time through i, minus LAG.
23 // primitive: entryOf(e) — the (key, window) pair this event belongs to.
25 // primitive: K — checkpoint every K events. K = 3
26 // primitive: CHECKPOINTS — where those land. CHECKPOINTS = [2, 5, 8]
28 // function: take(upto) — a checkpoint is the STATE and the OFFSET, together.
40 // function: restore(cp, useOffset) — resume. With the checkpoint's own offset the
41 // total is right; with a stale offset the prefix is applied twice.
45 for (id in cp.entries) { total = total + cp.entries[id] }
46 for (i in useOffset + 1 .. len(EVENTS) - 1) { total = total + EVENTS[i].v }
50 // primitive: countEntries(lo, hi) — distinct (key, window) pairs touched in that
54 // function: uploadVolume() — how many ENTRY-writes each checkpointing mode costs
55 // across the whole run. Full re-sends all of the state; incremental only churn.
68 // function: main() — THE CALLER: one checkpoint, two restores, one cost.
Step 1/0 — the checkpoint writes the state AND the offset
The Checkpoint carries `ent` and `upto` in one value — 4 entries holding 23, at offset 4. The offset is half the checkpoint, not metadata about it: a snapshot that does not
say where it was taken cannot be resumed from.

id = "a@240" (the loop over entries is done)
Step 2/0 — restoring with the matching offset gives the no-crash total
The loop starts at `useOffset + 1` = 5, so it adds the 4 events after the checkpoint to the 23 loaded from it: 45, the no-crash total. One expression, `useOffset + 1`, is
the entire correctness of the recovery.

Step 3/0 — and with a stale offset the prefix is counted twice
`restore(cp, 0)` replays from index 1, re-adding events already in `cp.entries`: 68 instead of 45, over by exactly the 23 the checkpoint had already accumulated. Same
state, same stream, one wrong argument.

Step 4/0 — incremental uploads churn; full uploads everything, every time
Compare the two accumulators' arguments: `countEntries(0, c)` grows with every checkpoint while `countEntries(prev + 1, c)` depends only on the gap. 14 against 8 here — and
the ratio keeps improving, because full tracks total state and incremental tracks churn.
